data.title: An Integrated Approach of PLS-SEM, Machine Learning, and SHAP to Predict the Adverse Effects of Generative AI Tools on Students’ Academic Performance in Higher Education Institutions

data.abstract: This study examines the destructive effects of generative AI (GAI) technologies on the academic performance of university students. Data were collected from 317 students at three public, four private and one Malaysian university using a structured questionnaire based on a 5-point Likert scale. The results of PLS-SEM algorithms reveal that AI dependency inception (ACI) has a significant positive effect on both adverse academic performance (AAP) (β = 0.17, t = 4.06, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.09, 0.25]), and cognitive skills reduction (CSR) (β = 0.16, t = 2.85, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.057, 0.283]). The mediation analysis showed that CSR mediates the relationship between ACI and AAP (β = 0.08, t = 2.83, p < 0.01, 95% CI [0.03, 0.15]). It was found that perceived institutional norms (PIN) influence AAP through technological distraction (TDN) (β = 0.07, t = 2.88, p < 0.01, 95% CI [0.03, 0.12]). Furthermore, we trained nine ML models to obtain predictions of AAP based on ACI, PIN, CSR and TDN features. It was found that Random Forest and Gradient Boosting performed the best in the metrics compared to other base models. The SHAP analysis showed that GAI tools were most strongly influenced by CSR, followed by TDN, PIN and ACI. The study emphasizes the need for logical AI integration, digital literacy and institutional policy measures to alleviate the overlooked academic implications of GAI usage in higher education institutions (HEIs).
